codeReview.summary: The fix resolves the original parity-lineage gap and adds explicit VAL-CROSS-004 execution evidence/checklist wiring, but it still does not enforce that smoke reproducibility was executed on an actual clean checkout of the cited commit.

issues.description: The script only checks commit existence via `git cat-file -t` and then runs all smoke checks in the current working tree; it never performs (or verifies) checkout/clone of the cited commit. This allows evidence to claim commit X while executing on a different checkout, so the original clean-checkout-on-cited-commit failure is not fully fixed. Related trust point: publication/traceability_check.py:327 only compares the JSON `commit_sha` field to memo text, not the actual execution checkout state.

If `claim_evidence_map.parity_run_ids` is present but unresolved, the checker silently falls back to `parity-artifacts/latest`. That weakens strict traceability because an undeclared/latest run can satisfy lineage checks when an explicitly referenced run is missing.

sharedStateObservations.observation: publication-worker guidance still does not explicitly require an executed clean-checkout smoke run on the cited commit, nor strict parity/benchmark/memo SHA equality enforcement behavior.
